title: From Hybrid Hydrological Models to Scalable Water Intelligence
content:
ABSTRACT

Hybrid hydrological modeling integrates process-based models with machine learning to advance knowledge across the hydrological cycle. By representing unresolved processes while retaining physical consistency, these approaches extend traditional hydrological models. However, improved predictive performance does not by itself create transferable or operational capabilities. Many implementations remain tied to specific basins, datasets, institutions, or computational environments, limiting reproducibility and operational uptake. We argue that the scaling challenge is not solely methodological, but also infrastructural, institutional, and economic. We propose a Scalable Hybrid Hydrological Modeling (SHHM) framework comprising four components: (1) modular and reusable model architectures, (2) harmonized multi-region datasets, (3) standardized community benchmarks, and (4) pathways from research tools to operational services. With appropriate human oversight, AI-enabled workflow automation can further scale SHHM by streamlining the end-to-end modeling lifecycle. International collaboration can strengthen SHHM when built on shared protocols, co-creation, reciprocal capacity building, transparent governance, and regionally relevant evaluation. This agenda shifts attention from isolated improvements in model performance toward the scientific, technical, and institutional capabilities required to deliver reliable, equitable, and operational water information in a changing water world.
